Development of a large-sample watershed-scale hydrometeorological data set for the contiguous USA: data set characteristics and assessment of regional variability in hydrologic model performance. Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci., 19, 209-223. doi:10.5194/hess-19-209-2015

Addor, N., Newman, A. J., Mizukami, N., and Clark, M. P. (2017). The CAMELS data set: catchment attributes and meteorology for large-sample studies. Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci., 21, 5293-5313. doi:10.5194/hess-21-5293-2017
licence_note: CAMELS-US streamflow originates from USGS NWIS (public domain); forcing is Daymet basin means as distributed by CAMELS.
access: read-only local copy; no network access during extraction
blob: data/et-budyko.json (inlined into module.html by scripts/build_modules.py as <script id="et-budyko">)
encoding: <column>_x100 in the blob = the value as distributed (two decimals) times 100, as integers; dayl_x100 holds the first value and then day-to-day differences (lossless)

all_gauges_table.rounding: each value rounded to 4 decimal places (to keep the page small); the four course basins are also stored unrounded under 'course'
all_gauges_table.na_handling: runoff_ratio is NA in camels_hydro for these gauge(s); stored as null and left out of the Budyko fit

units.daily: dayl s; srad W/m2 (mean over the daylight period); tmax, tmin C; vp Pa
units.attributes: p_mean, pet_mean, q_mean mm/day; aridity, runoff_ratio, frac_snow dimensionless

usage_note: PET is recomputed by the lesson from these forcing columns and compared with the tabulated pet_mean as a reproduction check; no modelOutput PET is used.
